https://nineoclock.ro/mariana-kuhnel-fma.text: ABOUT US NINE O’CLOCK STAFF 2024 COMMERCIAL OFFER – 2026 Subscribe to the Nine O’Clock 2026 CONTACT Special price offer 2026 with a 50% discount ASF President Alexandru Petrescu Holds Talks with FMA Board Member Mariana Kühnel in Bucharest Romanian-Austrian cooperation in the financial sector is being strengthened through closer dialogue between the supervisory authorities of the two countries. Mariana Kühnel, a member of the Executive Board of the Austrian Financial Market Authority (FMA), paid a working visit to Bucharest, where she held meetings with representatives of Romania’s key financial institutions. The agenda included meetings with Alexandru Petrescu, President of the Financial Supervisory Authority (ASF), Presidential Adviser Radu Burnete, and a Vice President of the National Bank of Romania (BNR). The discussions focused on the importance of close European cooperation and regular exchanges of information and expertise on financial market developments and supervision. The programme also included discussions with senior representatives of major Austrian companies listed on the stock exchange and active in Romania, highlighting the significant economic ties between the two countries. ASF President Alexandru Petrescu outlined the main topics discussed during his meeting with the FMA delegation in a post on his Facebook page: “Today, at the Authority’s headquarters, together with ASF First Vice President Gabriel-Ioan Avrămescu and Vice President of the Insurance-Reinsurance Sector Sorin Mititelu, I welcomed the delegation of the Austrian Financial Market Authority (FMA), which included Mariana Kühnel, Executive Director of the FMA, and Martina Andexlinger, Director of the Insurance Companies and Pension Funds Supervision Department. The meeting provided an opportunity for an in-depth exchange of views on the main developments and challenges in financial regulation and supervision at European level. Discussions focused on several strategic issues of common interest: ▶️ the status of implementation of the Insurance Recovery and Resolution Directive (IRRD) and the main challenges associated with its application; ▶️ developments concerning the Markets Integration and Supervision Package (MISP), including from the perspective of strengthening European capital markets and making the supervisory framework more efficient; ▶️ the experience of the two authorities and the challenges encountered in the field of crypto-assets, in the context of the evolving European regulatory and supervisory framework. I believe that direct dialogue between the competent national authorities is essential for strengthening the European Single Market and for underpinning our contributions to discussions within EIOPA and ESMA. Such meetings allow us to better understand common challenges, share experiences and best practices, and identify areas of convergence in addressing legislative and supervisory developments within the European Union. Cooperation with the FMA also has an important bilateral dimension, given the significant presence of Austrian groups and entities in Romania’s financial market. We will continue to deepen the excellent relationship between the two institutions and support an efficient exchange of information and expertise. In this way, we contribute to promoting high and convergent standards of regulation and supervision, strengthening institutional capacity, and maintaining stable, efficient and resilient financial markets in which participants can have confidence.” Mariana Kühnel’s visit to Bucharest comes at a time when European supervisory authorities are placing increasing emphasis on strengthening the Single Market and aligning regulatory and supervisory practices across Europe. The discussions on the implementation of the IRRD, developments concerning the Markets Integration and Supervision Package, and the challenges associated with crypto-assets highlight the need for close cooperation between national authorities, including through the regular exchange of experience and best practices. At the same time, the relationship between the ASF and the FMA has an important bilateral dimension, given the significant presence of Austrian groups and entities in Romania’s financial market.
